chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would go out until he looked at the horizons of the sky, and he said: 'Prayer should not be performed on that day on a carpet nor on a bare mat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using carpets or mats during Eid prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny) to perform Eid prayers in an open area, gazing toward the sky, which signifies the public and expansive nature of the celebration. The prohibition against using carpets (*bisat*) or mats (*bari*) during this specific prayer underscores a distinction from regular daily prayers, emphasizing simplicity and the communal aspect of the Eid gathering in open spaces rather than enclosed, decorated settings.
